Insurance

Group Medical Insurance for Employers

Group medical insurance lets an employer cover employees, and often their families, under one scheme. It supports hiring and retention, and the structure of the scheme matters as much as the premium: eligibility, limits, who pays for dependants and how claims are administered.

Request a quoteSpeak to an advisor

General information only. What is covered, the terms and the premium depend on the insurer’s policy wording, your circumstances and the information you disclose. Nothing here is a promise of cover.

What it covers

  • Inpatient and outpatient benefits for employees
  • Optional cover for spouses and children
  • Maternity, dental and optical, where included in the scheme design

Who needs it

  • SMEs and growing businesses
  • Schools, clinics and NGOs
  • Corporates reviewing existing schemes at renewal

Common risks

Cost creep at renewal

Claims experience and medical inflation influence renewals. Early review helps.

Inconsistent benefits

Different grades of staff may need different benefit tiers.

Important considerations and exclusions

  • Minimum group sizes and free cover limits vary by insurer.
  • Pre-existing condition treatment depends on scheme terms.

What affects the premium

  • Number of employees
  • Age and gender profile
  • Benefit design and limits
  • Claims history
  • Dependants covered

Premiums are set by insurers, so we do not publish figures. Tell us about your situation and we will explain what is driving the quotation.

What we need for a quotation

  • Employee count and demographic summary
  • Current benefits and renewal date
  • Claims experience summary, if available
  • Budget and priorities

How Chestnut can help

We explain the cover in plain language, collect the information insurers need, approach suitable insurers for terms, and help with renewals and claims. Policies are issued by insurers, and you decide what to buy.

Frequently asked questions

How early should we review before renewal?

Ideally two to three months. That leaves time to gather claims data and approach insurers.
